stories.headline: 45,000+ Samsung workers threaten history's largest chipmaker strike; government pursues emergency arbitration
stories.summary: More than 45,000 Samsung Electronics union workers announced an 18-day general strike beginning May 21 over bonus pay disputes, threatening to disrupt global DRAM and HBM chip supply. The South Korean government—from the prime minister down—declared a strike must be prevented at all costs, citing Samsung's share of national exports (22.8%) and potential daily losses near 1 trillion won; management entered emergency production mode, wound down wafer input, and Chairman Jay Y. Lee issued a public apology, while the union agreed to resume mediated talks on May 19.

stories.headline: Lee hosts US Treasury Secretary Bessent and Chinese VP He Lifeng ahead of US-China summit, emphasizes shipbuilding investment
stories.summary: President Lee Jae-myung met separately with US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng on May 13, one day before their principals' summit, urging stronger Korea-US strategic investment with shipbuilding as the centerpiece, and pressing China for 'tangible economic results.' Lee subsequently held a phone call with President Trump to discuss the outcomes of the US-China summit.

stories.headline: Lee and Mexican President Sheinbaum hold bilateral call on energy, trade, and a planned state visit
stories.summary: President Lee Jae-myung and Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum held a phone call on May 14 covering energy cooperation, bilateral trade investment, and cultural ties—including a discussion about BTS's visit to Mexico; Lee accepted Sheinbaum's invitation to visit Mexico in 2026. The call received extensive coverage in Mexican media.

stories.headline: AI 'citizen dividend' controversy: Lee defends policy aide against 'fake news' as PPP attacks and Bloomberg dispute emerges
stories.summary: A viral social media post by Blue House policy chief Kim Yong-beom proposing to redistribute AI-era tax windfalls to citizens as a 'national dividend' sparked political controversy; President Lee denounced media coverage as 'fake news' and 'subtle manipulation,' while the People Power Party accused Lee's office of pressuring Bloomberg over its related reporting. A Gallup Korea poll showed Lee's approval rating dipped 3 points to 61 percent amid the controversy.

stories.headline: Bank of Korea faces rate-hike pressure as inflation surges and won breaches 1,500 per dollar
stories.summary: South Korea's export and import prices surged sharply in April (40.8% and 20.2% YoY respectively) due to Middle East conflict-driven energy costs, pushing the Korean won past the psychologically important 1,500-per-dollar level for the first time since early April, spiking bond yields to two-year highs, and triggering growing market expectations that the Bank of Korea will hike rates. A new BOK board member acknowledged inflation risks are heightening, while foreign investor outflows from Korean securities continued for a third straight month.

stories.headline: BOK Governor Shin Hyun-song elected to BIS board; budget minister makes historic first visit to central bank
stories.summary: Bank of Korea Governor Shin Hyun-song was elected as a director on the Bank for International Settlements board at a BIS meeting in Basel on May 11, continuing South Korea's representation since 2019. Separately, Budget Minister Park Hong-keun made the first-ever visit by a budget minister to the Bank of Korea on May 14 to pledge fiscal-monetary policy coordination, symbolized by an exchange of symbolic gifts.

stories.headline: Korea-US defense dialogue addresses OPCON transfer gap and South Korea's potential Hormuz contribution
stories.summary: At the 28th Korea-US Integrated Defense Dialogue in Washington, Defense Minister Ahn Gyu-baek and Secretary Hegseth discussed wartime operational control (OPCON) transfer, with Ahn acknowledging a 'slightly different' timeline gap between the two allies; the ministers also agreed to deepen cooperation on shared security goals. Separately, Ahn outlined a 'phased' approach to possible South Korean support for US-led Strait of Hormuz security operations, stopping short of committing military personnel.

stories.headline: June 3 local elections: DPK maintains lead but PPP closes gap in Seoul, Busan, Daegu polls
stories.summary: Ahead of South Korea's June 3 local elections, polls show the ruling Democratic Party of Korea retaining wide leads nationally but PPP candidates have significantly narrowed gaps in Seoul (DPK 46% vs PPP 38%) and Busan (43% vs 41%) mayoral races. The DPK parliamentary leader urged voters to deliver a 'harsh judgment' on the PPP, while 513 uncontested DPK candidates were selected in strongholds, and former president Lee Myung-bak was seen endorsing PPP Seoul mayor candidate Oh Se-hoon.

stories.headline: Yoon Suk-yeol appeal trial halted after recusal request; Han Duck-soo challenges 15-year sentence
stories.summary: A Seoul appellate court suspended former President Yoon Suk-yeol's insurrection appeal trial on May 14 after his legal team filed a recusal request against judges who had previously ruled in former Prime Minister Han Duck-soo's appeal; Yoon and his lawyers did not appear for the hearing. Han Duck-soo, whose sentence was reduced from 23 to 15 years at appeal, separately filed his own further appeal challenging that verdict.

stories.headline: Lee backs expansionary 2027 budget and proactive fiscal policy, rejecting 'austerity trap'
stories.summary: At a cabinet meeting on May 12, President Lee Jae-myung directed officials to pursue a proactive fiscal stance in the second-half economic strategy and 2027 budget, explicitly rejecting what he called the 'populist fiscal austerity trap' and arguing that government investment is essential during global instability. Fitch separately affirmed South Korea has fiscal space thanks to the AI-driven semiconductor boom.

stories.summary: Following press criticism and President Lee's social-media amplification of reporting on 'Sangnoksu,' a private bad bank that has withheld debt forgiveness from 90,000+ borrowers since the 2003 credit card crisis, all nine major shareholder banks and card companies announced they would sell their delinquent receivables to the government's New Leap Fund—prompting the liquidation of Sangnoksu and releasing 110,000 borrowers from long-standing debt obligations.

stories.headline: North Korean women's soccer team arrives in South Korea for AFC tournament — first visit in eight years
stories.summary: Naegohyang Women's FC arrived at Incheon International Airport on May 18 to compete in the AFC Women's Champions League semifinals, marking the first visit by North Korean athletes to South Korea in eight years; the visit was authorized under the inter-Korean exchange law and drew heavy public interest, with all 7,087 public tickets sold. The match will not feature national symbols per AFC rules, and unification ministry officials cautioned against expecting a diplomatic thaw from the visit.

stories.headline: Lee and Japanese PM Takaichi plan Andong hometown summit focused on 'substantive cooperation'
stories.summary: South Korean President Lee Jae-myung and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi are scheduled to meet in Lee's hometown of Andong—a symbolic 'hometown diplomacy' gesture—to advance 'substantive cooperation' across a broad range of bilateral areas; the meeting follows their earlier January summit in Nara, Japan.

stories.headline: Hana Bank acquires $670M stake in Upbit operator Dunamu as South Korean banks push into crypto and stablecoins
stories.summary: Hana Financial Group announced a $670 million acquisition of a 6.55% stake in Dunamu, operator of South Korea's leading crypto exchange Upbit, with plans to co-develop a won-pegged stablecoin and blockchain-based remittances; the deal came as the ruling DPK proposed a Digital Asset Basic Act and South Korean domestic crypto holdings fell $41 billion over the past year as investors rotated into equities.

stories.headline: ROK Defense Ministry signs MOU with SK Telecom to deploy AI foundation model in military; KF-21 deployment nears as F-5 fleet retires
stories.summary: South Korea's Ministry of National Defense and SK Telecom signed an MOU on May 14 to develop a defense-specific AI model using SKT's Dokpamo foundation model—the first 'K-AI' deployment in the defense sector. Separately, the Air Force announced plans to retire its aging F-5 fighter jet fleet by end of 2027 as the domestically developed KF-21 Boramae fighter, whose first mass-production unit made its maiden flight in April 2026, nears operational deployment, though cost overruns have raised the Block-II program estimate nearly 30%.

stories.headline: KOSPI nears 8,000 as global investors pile into Korean stocks amid AI semiconductor boom
stories.summary: South Korea's benchmark KOSPI index approached the 8,000-point level during the week, drawing coverage in Japanese and US financial media of a 'Wall Street loves Korean stocks' trend; market capitalization of listed Korean firms grew approximately 4,500 trillion won in 11 months under the Lee administration. Citi moved to trim its bullish KOSPI position citing overheating risks, even as analysts raised price targets on Samsung and SK Hynix citing a structural memory supply shortage.

stories.headline: North Korea earned ~$14B from Russia war support in three years; NK operatives steal $2B targeting financial firms
stories.summary: A research institute affiliated with South Korea's National Intelligence Service, citing Bank of Korea data, estimated North Korea earned up to $14 billion over three years by supplying weapons and troops to Russia—equivalent to roughly half of North Korea's annual GDP. Separately, a CrowdStrike report found North Korean cyber operatives stole $2 billion in 2025, with financial services firms identified as the primary next target.

stories.headline: Lee's approval rating slides to 61%, then 59.7%, amid citizen dividend controversy
stories.summary: Gallup Korea polling released on May 15 showed President Lee Jae-myung's approval rating fell 3 percentage points to 61 percent, ending a seven-week streak above 60 percent, with the decline attributed to the citizen dividend controversy; an earlier Realmeter survey from May 11 had shown a rebound to 59.7 percent driven by stock market gains.
